public_rationale: OpenAI’s August 1 release supports Marcus’s cautious impression of strength on open problems. The theory-building clause remains unsettled. The original manuscript claims a new technical ingredient, but that alone neither establishes theory building nor rules it out. Tao’s general distinction cannot establish the absence of Astra-specific evidence. The search found no decisive contemporary demonstration or comprehensive assessment of that absence.
limitations: The principal results source is the model developer.
The mathematical proofs and formalizations were not independently verified in this assessment.
Theory building and inventive proof construction have an uncertain boundary.
Later achievements cannot directly refute the August 3 public-evidence claim.

our_interpretation: Astra means the internal OpenAI model identified in the mathematical results announcement discussed by the post.
The cautious phrase 'seems strong' requires credible demonstrated successes, not universal reliability or a specified benchmark score.
Building theory means developing useful mathematical concepts, definitions, or frameworks beyond completing an individual proof. It need not mean creating an entire discipline.
'No evidence thus far' concerns publicly available evidence through August 3, 2026, not permanent inability or undisclosed internal work.
The target is the public evidence record through publication. Its beginning is unspecified, so target_period.start is null.
